title: CI benchmark matrix for driver/CUDA images + regression alerting
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Goal: Establish a reproducible CI benchmark matrix that validates combinations of NVIDIA driver, CUDA toolkit, and pinned container images across runner types (GH self-hosted, k8s GPU node pools) and surfaces token/sec and p95 regressions automatically. The matrix should be cheap for PRs (smoke) and comprehensive nightly for full coverage. It must produce stable baselines, attach metadata (image tag, driver version, kernel, GPU type), and trigger alerts when predefined performance SLOs regress. This ticket scopes the CI orchestration, telemetry plumbing, threshold logic, and an initial set of golden images and runner configs.
acceptance_criteria: A nightly CI matrix run executes across the selected combos and writes results to perf-store (S3 prefix) with metadata keys: image_tag, driver_version, cudatoolkit, gpu_type, kernel_version, run_id.
PR-triggered smoke benchmark runs (single GPU type + latest driver) complete in <20 minutes and block merges only if a hard regression is detected.
Datadog dashboards ingest tokens/sec and p95 metrics with tags matching metadata and historical baselines are visualized.
Regression detection rules: tokens/sec drop >8% vs baseline OR p95 latency increase >10% for the same workload triggers a warning; >15% drop or >20% p95 increase triggers a critical PagerDuty alert.
Pinning strategy documented and a set of 'golden' container images published (example tag: redwood/bench:ci-2025-02-05-cuda12.1-driver535) with corresponding git-backed image manifests.
Compatibility checks run for at least A100 and H100 node pools; failures create a reproducible issue template and link to the failed run artifacts.
Run metadata and raw traces link back to the originating GitHub PR or nightly run in the CI UI for triage.
tasks: Define canonical matrix axes (driver_version, cudatoolkit, image_tag, gpu_type, runner_type).
Build and publish initial golden images for CUDA 11.8, 12.0, 12.1 pinned to specific driver versions (e.g., driver-535, driver-540).
Implement small-fast smoke harness for PRs that replays a short token-generation workload (10k tokens total) and emits tokens/sec + p95 metrics.
Create nightly full harness that runs synthetic and production replay workloads across A100/H100/T4 node pools.
Plumb Datadog metrics ingestion with required tags; add dashboards and saved views for comparison to baseline.
Implement regression detection lambda that compares latest run to baseline in perf-store and posts results to Datadog events and Slack + PagerDuty according to severity thresholds.
Add CI gating logic: allow PR to opt-in for full runs via label; always run smoke by default.
Document image pinning policy and kernel/driver compatibility matrix in Confluence.

notes: Decision: store baselines as time-windowed artifacts in S3 (perf-store) keyed by workload_id + image_tag; baseline window = last 7 successful nightly runs.
Tradeoff: running full matrix nightly is costly — mitigated by sampling (run all GPU types but sample fewer driver combinations on non-critical nights).
Tradeoff: smoke runs on PR are necessarily noisy; we will allow a higher tolerance for PR gating and reserve strict checks for nightly runs.
Implementation detail: use nvidia-smi --query and container runtime introspection to capture driver/kernel metadata at test start; store alongside metrics.
Monitoring: Datadog metric names = bench.tokens_per_sec, bench.p95_ms with tags env:ci, run:nightly|pr, image_tag:<tag>, driver:<v>, cudatoolkit:<v>, gpu:<type>.
Run retention policy: keep full trace artifacts 30 days, metered aggregates 365 days.
Follow-ups: integrate perf CI results into PR UI with a small status summary and link to the failing workload artifacts for triage.
